analysis.object_name: Tubular object with forked tip and D-shaped side opening - whistle-like / hollow-gouge-like appearance
analysis.summary: Close-up angled front view of a single dark tubular foreground object against a white background. Visible features include a cylindrical body, a large D-shaped side cutout revealing a hollow interior, and a notched tip forming two prongs with flat, textured end faces.

components.name: Outer tubular body
components.function: Forms main enclosure and structural support for the object
components.evidence: Dark cylindrical exterior extending from right edge toward center, with smooth curved side and reflective highlight

components.name: D-shaped side aperture
components.function: Opening in the tube wall that may allow air, light, or material interaction with the hollow interior
components.evidence: Clearly defined D-shaped cutout on upper side of tube with bright beveled rim
material_candidates: same as body with exposed edge

components.name: Forked / notched tip with two prongs
components.function: Forward extension of the tube walls creating a U-shaped notch
components.evidence: Two protruding rectangular prongs at leftmost end with the gap between them aligned with the side aperture

components.name: Textured flat end faces
components.function: Terminal surfaces of the prongs, possibly cutting edges, striking surfaces, or protective caps
components.evidence: Light-colored, rough granular texture visible on the very front faces of both prongs

components.name: Hollow interior channel
components.function: Empty space inside the tube visible through the side aperture and tip notch
components.evidence: Dark interior void and a lighter curved inner wall seen through the side opening and between the prongs

principles.name: Tubular shell stiffness
principles.explanation: A hollow cylindrical form can resist bending while remaining lightweight; here the side cutout and tip notch would locally reduce that stiffness but are part of the visible geometry, involving part-1, part-2, part-3

principles.name: Opening to interior interaction
